samples.summary: `stoodDown` is latched per-subject and never reset, so a document that once stood down stays permanently non-durable while still holding the election lock
samples.evidence:
`const [stoodDown, setStoodDown] = useState<string | null>(null)` (line 239) is written only by `giveUp` (line 241) and read at line 250 (`stoodDown !== subject`). Grepping the whole frontend for `setStoodDown` finds exactly one call site — there is no reset when `subject` changes or when the document re-mounts.

Consequence: after `onLockRefused` fires for subject S (`7:note-7`), the user navigates to another document and back to `note-7`. `held.current` is re-latched for S (line 246-248), and `useDurableDocument`'s effect re-runs for the new/old docKey and **re-acquires** the `wb-durable:7:note-7` Web Lock (use-durable-document.ts:192-221, which has no memory of the stand-down — `standDown` only mutated `decision`, not `latched`/`eligible`). But `decided` is `undefined` because `stoodDown === subject` is still true from the first visit, so `CollabDocumentProvider` returns `inner` (line 305-307) and never mounts `DurableYorkieProvider`.

That is exactly the state this feature's own test asserts must not happen (`collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx` → "takes no election it is not going to use": "Holding `wb-durable:{user}:{docKey}` without mounting a client denies durability to every other tab for nothing"). Here the lock is held for the life of the open document, and no other tab can be the durable one for it, while this tab persists nothing.

samples.summary: A `['me','optional']` refetch that resolves to `null` (expired session) tears down the durable subtree and remounts `DocumentProvider`, discarding the in-memory Yorkie change queue the feature exists to protect
samples.evidence:
Line 305: `if (!decided?.durable || !decided.clientKey || !me) return inner;`. `me` comes from `useQuery({queryKey:['me','optional'], queryFn: fetchMeOptional, retry:false})` (line 185-192), and `fetchMeOptional` resolves `null` when there is no valid session (api/auth.ts:171 "Returns null when there is no valid session").

React Query refetches on window focus by default. If the cookie expires while an editor sits open with unsent edits, the refetch resolves `null`, `me` becomes null, and two things happen at once: `subject` (line 233) flips from `7:note-7` to `anon:note-7`, re-latching `held.current` with `durable:false`, and the `!me` term short-circuits to `return inner`. `inner` is a *different element type at the same position* than the `<DurableYorkieProvider>{inner}</DurableYorkieProvider>` branch, so React unmounts `DocumentProvider` and the whole editor under it.

The file's own doc comment (lines 208-222) states this is precisely the loss the latch exists to prevent: "switching between them unmounts the `DocumentProvider` and the entire editor subtree under it — discarding the Yorkie change queue, which on a document with unsent edits is the loss this whole feature exists to prevent." The latch handles a preference flip but not `me → null`. A *different* user signing in is a deliberate re-decide; a session simply expiring is not, and there is no guard distinguishing them.

samples.summary: `purgeDocument`'s archive drop ignores the `skipOpen` and `updatedSince` guards, so the reconcile can delete an archive — the only copy of unreconciled work — for a document its own guards just spared
samples.evidence:
In `purgeDocument` (lines 885-905) the `skipOpen` and `updatedSince` checks are inside the per-live-entry loop (lines 886-892), but `if (options.archives === "drop") { await this.dropArchivesForDocument(documentId); }` (line 902) runs unconditionally afterwards, outside both guards.

`purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` (offline-erase.ts:401-405) calls it with `{archives:'drop', skipOpen:true, updatedSince: listedAt}` for every id absent from a listing taken a moment ago. So a document that is `isLive` in another tab, or whose entry was touched after `listedAt`, keeps its live entry but loses its archive. An archive is by this feature's own design the only durable copy of work the SDK could not reconcile (offline-copy.ts header comment), so the loss is unrecoverable. The guards were added precisely because the listing's absence is a guess, not an answer — the same reasoning applies to the archive, which is the more valuable of the two.

samples.summary: `purgeOfflineDocuments` wraps the whole id loop in one try, so a failure on the first id silently skips every remaining id
samples.evidence: Lines 320-330: the `for (const id of documentIds) { await store.purgeDocument(...) }` loop sits inside a single `try`, whose `catch` only logs. A transient IndexedDB failure on id[0] abandons ids[1..n], leaving local copies of documents the server has already deleted on the disk, with no retry and no record that anything was skipped. The next reconcile would only catch them if they are also absent from the server listing (which they would be), so it degrades rather than loses data — but the per-id work should be independently guarded, as `retryPendingOfflineErase` (lines 283-297) already does for its own loop.

samples.summary: The fallback store created by `watchForOfflineDisable` is never closed, leaking an open IndexedDB connection that can block a later `deleteDatabase`/version change
samples.evidence: Line 458: `const current = store() ?? new WafflebaseDocStore({ userId: who });` — when the caller has no store (the Settings route case this fallback exists for), a fresh store is constructed, used by `eraseOfflineData` at line 466, and never `.close()`d. Every other construction site in this module (`eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` line 263, `retryPendingOfflineErase` line 295, `purgeOfflineDocuments` line 329, `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` line 412) closes in a `finally`. The store's own doc comment explains why closing matters: "Closes the connection, so a `deleteDatabase` elsewhere is not blocked" (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:494).

samples.summary: `collectStale` sweeps every account's entries but asks a liveness question scoped to one account, and its `purge` does not mark the key, so another account's open document can be collected silently
samples.evidence:
`collectStale` deliberately collects entries for all users (line 1129 `headerKeysWhere(BY_UPDATED_AT, range)` is unscoped, see the comment at 1106-1113), but the liveness test at line 1132 is `this.isLive(docKey)`, which consults `this.touched` (this instance) and `this.isOpenElsewhere` — wired in offline-runtime.tsx:71-72 as `isOpenInAnyTab(docKey, { userId, whenUnknown: false })`, i.e. scoped to the *signed-in* user. Another account's document held open in another tab therefore answers "not open" and is purged.

Unlike `dropAllForUser` (line 1071) and `purgeDocument` (line 899), the collection path calls `this.purge(docKey)` (line 1137) without `this.evicted.add(docKey)`, so that other tab's next `appendChange` finds no header and takes the contract's silent "no base" success (lines 633-635, 653-656) — every subsequent edit goes nowhere while its chip still reports the document saved. Reachability is low because `load()` touches `updatedAt` on attach, so an open document is rarely 30 days stale; but nothing structurally prevents it.

samples.summary: The module-global `evictedKeys` set grows for the life of the page and is never trimmed
samples.evidence: `const evictedKeys = new Map<string, Set<string>>()` (line ~344) accumulates a key on every eviction, `purgeDocument` and `dropAllForUser`. Only `saveSnapshot` removes one (line 598). Keys purged by the reconcile or by logout for documents that are never reopened stay in the set forever. Unbounded in principle, trivial in practice.

No guard elsewhere makes this unreachable; the only mitigating factor is that the trigger (`onLockRefused`, durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:306-309) is a race backstop, which affects severity, not reality. Broken invariant / stale latched state is in the correctness lane.

finding.summary: Enabling offline persistence while an editor is open unmounts the DocumentProvider, discarding the unsent change queue
finding.evidence: `if (!ready) return null;` (line 273) runs on every render, with `ready = settled && identified`. `settled` comes from `useDurableDocument`, where `settled: !eligible || answered` and `answered = decision?.subject === subject` with `subject = `${eligible}\0${userId}\0${docKey}`` (use-durable-document.ts:179, 225, 247). When the preference flips from off to on for an already-open document, `eligibleNow` rises (the latch at use-durable-document.ts:161-163 deliberately allows rising), `subject` changes, `answered` becomes false and `settled` becomes false — so `ready` is false and `CollabDocumentProvider` returns `null`, unmounting `DocumentProvider` and the whole editor subtree in that commit, before the election effect can resolve. The file's own comment (lines 204-218) states that unmounting the `DocumentProvider` "discard[s] the Yorkie change queue, which on a document with unsent edits is the loss this whole feature exists to prevent". This is reachable from the advertised flow: the sync chip only offers `Turn on for later documents` while `state === 'not-saved'`, i.e. precisely when unsent edits exist (sync-status-chip.tsx:146, 240) — so clicking the offer destroys the work it was warning about. It also fires for every open editor when the toggle is flipped in Settings or in another tab. The existing durable suite only covers the preference being turned *off* mid-open ('keeps its client when the preference changes underneath it'), never turned on.

verdict.reason: The finding's two load-bearing claims do not match the code. (1) The gate is not `if (!ready) return null;` — collab-document-provider.tsx:301-303 reads `if (!ready && held.current?.subject !== subject) return null;`, i.e. a pre-decision gate. `held` is latched at lines 246-248 on the first ready render for `subject = `${me?.id ?? 'anon'}:${docKey}`` (line 233), which does not include the offline preference; so once an editor is mounted for a user+doc, `held.current.subject === subject` and the `return null` branch is unreachable regardless of `settled`/`identified` flipping. (2) The eligibility latch in use-durable-document.ts:166-171 is keyed on `identity = ${userId}\0${docKey}` only — `eligibleNow` is NOT part of the key — so eligibility is held in both directions and cannot rise mid-open. Therefore `subject` (line 186) does not change and `settled` (line 254) does not go false when the preference is turned on for an already-open document. Both the comment at collab-document-provider.tsx:290-296 and at use-durable-document.ts:144-160 describe exactly this defence. The only reachable `return null` is before any DocumentProvider (and hence any change queue) exists. Code is not present as described.

mergedFrom.summary: Election acquired but never used after the preference is enabled mid-open, blocking a second tab from durability

finding.summary: An election is acquired but never used when eligibility rises after the provider latched non-durable, holding the per-document lock and denying durability to every other tab
finding.evidence: `held.current` is written once per `subject` (`${me.id}:${docKey}`) on the first `ready` render and never revisited (collab-document-provider.tsx:242-248), while `useDurableDocument` keeps re-deciding: its `latched` eligibility is allowed to *rise* (use-durable-document.ts:159-163) and the effect then calls `acquireDurableSession` and holds `wb-durable:{user}:{docKey}` until unmount. So when the preference is switched on while a document is open — which is the chip's own primary entry point (`turnOnOfflineSaving`, sync-status-chip.tsx:148) — this tab takes and keeps the election for a document it will never persist. Any other tab that opens the same document is refused the election (`acquireDurableSession` returns undefined) and stays non-durable, so the feature the user just enabled silently does not work for that document in any tab until the holding tab closes it.

verdict.reason: The finding's load-bearing premise — that `useDurableDocument`'s latched eligibility is "allowed to rise" — is not present in the code. The latch at use-durable-document.ts:166-171 is keyed solely on `identity = ${userId}�${docKey}`, which contains no preference-derived term, so flipping the offline preference mid-open leaves `latched.current.eligible` unchanged (held in both directions). The lines the reviewer cites (159-163) are comment prose explaining why a rise is deliberately disallowed, not code permitting one. The sole product-code call to `acquireDurableSession` (use-durable-document.ts:205) sits behind the `!eligible` early return at :197 in an effect with deps `[eligible, userId, docKey, subject]` (:221); none of those deps move on a preference flip, so no `wb-durable:{user}:{docKey}` lock is ever taken for a document the provider latched non-durable. The provider's own latch key `${me?.id ?? 'anon'}:${docKey}` (collab-document-provider.tsx:233) moves in lockstep with the hook's identity (userId passed at :205), so the claimed divergence cannot arise. The exact claimed scenario is asserted to behave the opposite way in use-durable-document.test.tsx:156-181 (`expect(locks.held.size).toBe(0)` after enabling mid-open), and the chip's toast (sync-status-chip.tsx:87-97) documents the same "next document opened" semantics.

finding.summary: An involuntary 401 erases the local live entries, which include the un-pushed change log — destroying the only durable copy of unsent work
finding.evidence: `fetchWithAuth`'s 401 arm calls `logout({... eraseLocalData: "keep-archives"})`, which reaches `dropAllForUser(userId, {keepArchives:true})` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1031). That loop calls `this.purge(docKey)` for every header, and `purge` deletes the CHANGES range as well as the snapshot. The justification in the comment — "The live entries still go. They are copies of content the server holds, so nothing is lost by dropping them" — is false for the log: the store's own eviction logic says the opposite (`evictOldest` skips any entry with `changeCount > 0` because "this store cannot tell an acked change from an unacked one", wafflebase-doc-store.ts). So a session that expires (or any transient 401 from a restarted backend) while a durable document holds un-pushed edits deletes exactly the work the feature exists to preserve; the redirect to /login is refusable (see the `redirectTo` comment about `beforeunload`, auth.ts:47-60), so the tab can keep running and then lose the edits on the next reload.

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. The finding claims the 401 arm of `fetchWithAuth` passes `eraseLocalData: "keep-archives"` and thereby reaches `dropAllForUser(userId, {keepArchives:true})`, purging live entries and their un-pushed change log. In the repository, `LogoutOptions.eraseLocalData` is typed `"all" | "none"` (auth.ts:34) and the string "keep-archives" does not exist anywhere (grep returns no hits). The 401 arm passes `eraseLocalData: "none"` (auth.ts:277), and `logout()` gates the erase with `if (eraseLocalData !== "none" && res?.ok)` (auth.ts:134), so `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` is never invoked on an involuntary 401 — no store is opened, no `dropAllForUser` runs, and no `purge` touches the CHANGES range. Furthermore the only logout-side caller, `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout`, calls `eraseOfflineData(store, who)` with no options (offline-erase.ts:244), so nothing passes `keepArchives` at all. The `keepArchives` parameter and its comment at wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1047/1078-1085 are now unused documentation, not a reachable data-loss path. The `redirectTo`/`beforeunload` reasoning cited is real (auth.ts:47-74) but is only harmful if an erase occurred, which it does not.

finding.summary: After a sign-out erase the still-mounted durable client re-persists the document to disk; the only write guard is the preference, not the sign-out
finding.evidence: The store is built with `isPersistenceEnabled: getOfflinePersistenceEnabled` and nothing else. `refuseIfDisabled` therefore only blocks writes when the *preference* is off. On the 401 path, `dropAllForUser` purges the entries and marks them evicted, so the client's next `appendChange` throws — which makes the SDK write a fresh `saveSnapshot`, and `saveSnapshot` does `this.evicted.delete(docKey)` and writes the document back (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:580-600). Because the 401 redirect is refusable (auth.ts:47-60: a `beforeunload` guard — which the sync chip registers precisely when there are unsent edits — lets the user cancel and the page keeps running), the erase promised on sign-out is undone and a signed-out account's document content is back on a possibly shared disk, with nothing scheduled to remove it again.

verdict.reason:
The finding's core evidence claim is factually wrong. It asserts the store is constructed with `isPersistenceEnabled: getOfflinePersistenceEnabled` "and nothing else", so only the preference gates writes. The actual code at durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:172-173 is `isPersistenceEnabled: () => getOfflinePersistenceEnabled() && isOfflineWritePermitted(userId)` — the sign-out-specific conjunct the reviewer says is missing is present, and the comment at lines 159-171 documents exactly the hazard raised.

The guard is complete end-to-end: eraseOfflineDataOnLogout calls denyOfflineWrites(who) after a successful erase (offline-erase.ts:256, with comments at 251-255 naming the same re-persist scenario); denyOfflineWrites adds to the `erased` set (offline-erase.ts:120-125) so isOfflineWritePermitted returns false (offline-erase.ts:137-139); and saveSnapshot calls refuseIfDisabled(docKey) as its first statement (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:581), before compression or any transaction, so the SDK's "fresh snapshot" repair throws and never reaches `this.evicted.delete(docKey)` at line 598. appendChange (623) and saveMeta (670) are guarded identically. The predicate is evaluated at write time, not captured at construction, so a denial recorded after the store was built still restrains the still-mounted client.

The specific reachability path the finding relies on is also absent: logout only calls eraseOfflineDataOnLogout() when `eraseLocalData !== "none" && res?.ok` (auth.ts:134-136), and the 401 arm passes "none" (auth.ts:31-34, 129-133). On the refusable-redirect path described, no erase runs, so there is nothing for a re-persist to undo. The beforeunload/redirect-latch code at auth.ts:47-74 is quoted accurately but does not carry the harm, because both other links in the chain are not as described.

One narrower residual exists that the finding did not raise: if dropAllForUser throws partway, some keys are purged and marked evicted while denyOfflineWrites is skipped (offline-erase.ts:257-261). That is a different claim from "the only write guard is the preference", which is what was filed and what the repository contradicts.
